web/case-study.html.old: A ride record alone does not establish a complete claim. This build assembles the support, keeps missing facts visible and traces what each claim can support downstream.
web/case-study.html.new:
A ride record alone does not establish a complete claim.

  • Build the support: assemble claim facts while keeping gaps visible.
  • Trace the consequence: show what that claim can support downstream.

web/case-study.html.old:
The operational problem begins upstream of encounter reporting. A source can describe a completed ride while leaving the claim's billing reference, supported service quantity or required payment evidence unresolved. Producing a report from that activity requires an explicit claim record and a rule for what makes it usable.

The model keeps four questions distinct. A ride describes activity. A claim assembles supported facts. Readiness asks whether those facts meet a particular target's requirements. Return evidence establishes what a recipient actually said about the submitted version.
